subject: Follow-up: Integration & RSP schema clarifications
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: RSP schema & streaming semantics

Thanks for the call this morning — good overview. A few follow-ups from our side as we start the integration planning: 

1) SDK & auth: are we expected to use a static API key for server-to-server traffic, or do you recommend short-lived tokens / OAuth for service accounts? We need this for our security review.

2) Chat vs completions: for our multi-turn product support assistant, is the chat endpoint the recommended path (maintain convo state + tool calling)? Any guidance on token accounting across messages?

3) Tokenization / max_tokens: what is the recommended approach for truncation and stop sequences when we send structured output schemas (we plan to use JSON schema enforcement / tool calling)?

4) Streaming semantics: if we stream responses for user-facing latency, how should we handle partial structured outputs and post-processing (i.e., when tool-calls or JSON is emitted incrementally)?

5) Embeddings + re-rankers: quick Q — is it better to run reranking as a separate embeddings similarity step followed by a completion, or to use a single prompt with embedded context + reranker instruction?

Could you give short recommendations and any sample SDK snippets or a link to the schema doc? Also cc'ing our engineering lead Sofia — she may have more detailed infra questions.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
CTO, Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T13:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: RSP schema & streaming semantics

Hi Daniel / Sofia — great speaking with you all. Below are concise recommendations and links; happy to sync if you'd like a short tech-to-tech session.

1) SDK & auth
- For server-to-server calls we support both long-lived API keys and short-lived tokens. For enterprise/private deployments we typically recommend short-lived tokens (our SDKs integrate with customer KMS/OAuth flows) — better for rotation and audit. Rishi (cc) can share our example exchange flow for service accounts.

2) Chat vs Completions
- Use the chat endpoint for multi-turn assistants and any flows that require tool calling / structured output across turns. The chat model keeps an explicit message list and KV cache semantics; token accounting includes all messages in the current context window.
- Use completions for single-shot or simple instruction tasks where you control the full prompt.

3) Tokenization / max_tokens / stop
- We recommend computing token counts client-side using our tokenizer utility in the SDK (see link below) so you can reserve headroom for structured fields.
- For structured JSON output, use the schema/tool-calling mechanism: the model will emit the JSON as a single object when possible. If you rely on stop sequences, be careful: stops are string-based and may split across token boundaries. Prefer schema enforcement (tool-calling) for exactness.
- max_tokens should be set to the expected output + buffer; for streaming, low buffers may truncate final structures.

4) Streaming semantics for structured output
- Streaming returns token deltas. For JSON/tool calls you may get partial fragments. Our SDK exposes a "json_stream_buffer" helper (see snippet in the doc) that accumulates tokens and attempts incremental JSON parse; it emits a validated object only once complete. If a tool call is detected mid-stream, the SDK will surface the tool name and partial args, and you can wait for the final tool payload.

5) Embeddings + rerankers
- Recommended pattern for high-quality reranking: 1) retrieve candidate docs via embedding similarity, 2) build a compact prompt with top-K candidates, 3) run a reranker/comparator completion to score or select. This separates concerns and scales better. A single large prompt with all context can work but is more brittle and costly.

Routing / Model Variants
- If you need latency SLOs, route traffic to a smaller quantized variant for low-latency inference and fall back to a higher-accuracy variant for heavy batches. Dev can share routing policy examples.

Next steps
- Can you share a sample request payload (input text, expected structured schema, QPS and latency SLO)? I attached a small example payload file for reference.
- If you want, we can schedule a 30-min tech session with Rishi + Dev to walk the sample and SDK integration.

Helpful links:
- Integration spec: https://redwood-inference.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/eng/Acme-RSP-Specs
- SDK tokenization helper: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk#tokenizer
- Reranking pattern doc: https://redwood-inference.internal/docs/rerank-patterns

Attachments: example_payload.json (stub)

Best,
Marissa Cole
